evals.name: core-project-detected
expectations: The response identifies that the project uses 2D Physics Core, based on the script in the prompt
The ball is created through the Unity.U2D.Physics API, such as PhysicsWorld.defaultWorld and CreateBody, not with Rigidbody2D or CircleCollider2D
The ball's body type is set explicitly to dynamic
The code does not use the UnityEngine.LowLevelPhysics2D namespace

evals.name: legacy-project-detected
expectations: The response identifies that the project uses the Rigidbody 2D system, based on the script in the prompt
The jump is applied to the existing Rigidbody2D, through AddForce or by setting its linearVelocity
The response does not use any Unity.U2D.Physics types

evals.name: no-signal-asks
evals.prompt: Add physics to the crates in my 2D game so the player can knock them over.
expectations: The response asks which 2D physics system to use before writing any physics code
It offers three routes: legacy components (Rigidbody 2D and Collider 2D), 2D Physics Core components, and 2D Physics Core in script
It notes that the 2D Physics Core components need the com.unity.2d.physics package
It does not pick a system on the user's behalf

evals.name: core-bulk-script
evals.prompt: Using 2D Physics Core in script, spawn 50 dynamic circles above a static ground.
expectations: The code uses PhysicsWorld.defaultWorld rather than creating a new world
Body types are set with the type property and PhysicsBody.BodyType, Static for the ground and Dynamic for the circles
The code does not use the obsolete bodyType property or RigidbodyType2D
Types come from the Unity.U2D.Physics namespace, not UnityEngine.LowLevelPhysics2D
The code does not use Rigidbody2D, CircleCollider2D or any other legacy component

evals.name: legacy-missing-collider
evals.prompt: My sprite has a Rigidbody 2D but drops straight through the ground. How do I fix it?
expectations: The response says the sprite needs a Collider 2D component, such as a BoxCollider2D or CircleCollider2D
The response says the ground also needs a Collider 2D
The response stays in the Rigidbody 2D system and does not suggest 2D Physics Core types
The response does not suggest 3D components such as Rigidbody or BoxCollider

evals.name: core-hinge-degrees
evals.prompt: In 2D Physics Core script, hang a dynamic body from a static anchor with a hinge joint, and limit its swing to between -45 and 45 degrees.
expectations: The joint is created through the Unity.U2D.Physics API, not with HingeJoint2D
The anchor body is static and the swinging body is dynamic
The angle limits are given as -45 and 45 degrees, not converted to radians

evals.name: legacy-ground-raycast
evals.prompt: Check whether my 2D player is grounded with a raycast straight down that only hits the Ground layer. The player uses a Rigidbody 2D.
expectations: The raycast uses Physics2D.Raycast, not Physics.Raycast
The raycast is limited to the Ground layer with a layer mask
The code checks the returned RaycastHit2D for a hit, through its collider or its implicit bool conversion
No 2D Physics Core types are used

evals.name: legacy-trigger-not-firing
evals.prompt: OnTriggerEnter2D never fires when my player walks into a coin. Both have a BoxCollider2D and the coin's is set to Is Trigger.
expectations: The response says at least one of the two objects needs a Rigidbody 2D for trigger messages to be sent
The response stays in the Rigidbody 2D system and does not suggest 2D Physics Core or 3D physics

evals.name: core-debug-visuals
evals.prompt: How do I see the shapes of the bodies I create with the 2D Physics Core API while debugging?
expectations: The response points to 2D Physics Core's own physics renderer or the world's draw options
It does not suggest Gizmos or Debug.DrawLine
It does not suggest adding a GameObject or sprite to see the bodies

evals.name: core-old-namespace
evals.prompt: My project uses Unity 6000.3. In 2D Physics Core script, create a dynamic box body that falls onto a static ground.
expectations: The code uses the UnityEngine.LowLevelPhysics2D namespace, not Unity.U2D.Physics
The ground body is set to static and the box body to dynamic
The code does not use Rigidbody2D, BoxCollider2D or any other legacy component
